finding: Topbar coverage on editor-chrome boards is already complete: every board that draws the editor shell carries the Topbar component, and no board draws the rail without it. The component is doing its job — the defects below are inside it, not in its reach.
evidence: Page 1:3 holds 520 top-level boards (519 FRAME + 1 COMPONENT_SET; 367 TEXT captions and 12 RECTANGLEs are not boards). 149 are 1440 wide. 102 carry an INSTANCE whose mainComponent.parent is 681:122 — 101 of them 1440x56, one 1280x56, all at x=0,y=0. Cross-tabbed against the Rail set 2034:8519: BOTH rail+topbar = 99 boards, rail-without-topbar = 0, topbar-without-rail = 3 (65:211 Shell state 7 · Preview, 1688:7195 S7 · Settings · root, 807:8663 S3.8 · preview-responsive · mobile-device-frame — all three surfaces that legitimately drop the rail).
recommend: No coverage work needed. Spend the effort on D-N-05 through D-N-09, which are defects inside the 102 instances.

screen: 48 boards at 1440 with no Topbar instance
finding: The 48 topbar-less 1440-wide boards are not gaps: 8 are annotation strips and 38 are overlay-only boards that deliberately draw a scrim+modal over an implied editor. Only 2 are real exceptions. But the overlay convention is itself split down the middle — 19 draw a scrim and 19 do not.
evidence: Classified all 48 by height and direct children. STRIPS (height != 900/852) = 8: 307:2223 (1440x140), 876:4532 (1163), 1344:7162 (400), 813:4836 (360), 1342:7162 (360), 814:7027 (320), 1345:7162 (480), 817:4649 (500). OVERLAY with a scrim child = 19 (e.g. 183:2 kids=scrim:1440,modal/440:440; 184:2 scrim+modal/560; 307:2193 scrim+Frame:520). OVERLAY with NO scrim = 19 (e.g. 294:1976 kids=Frame:480 only; 302:1978 kids=Frame:580 only; 807:7252 kids=modal:720 only; 296:1972 kids=checklist:340 only). GAPS = 2: 1343:7162 and 807:8723 (see D-N-03).
recommend: Pick one overlay convention and apply it to all 38. A scrim is the thing that tells a reader the board is an overlay rather than a screen missing its chrome — the 19 scrim-less boards (294:1976, 294:1984, 294:1992, 295:1972, 296:1972, 296:1999, 296:2030, 302:1978, 302:2004, 302:2026, 807:7252, 807:8756, 807:8787, 813:4888 + 5 already-retired) read as broken screens today.

finding: Exactly one detached topbar exists on page 1:3 — a local FRAME named 'Topbar (view mode)' — and it is detached for a real reason: it is a different composition the component set cannot currently express. It needs a Mode axis, not a re-attach.
evidence: 1343:7163 FRAME 'Topbar (view mode)' 1440x56, 4 children: TEXT '‹ Back to editing' @24, TEXT 'Bella Cucina' @170, FRAME 'lifecycle pill' 120x24 @280 reading 'Opened · no reply', TEXT '💬 🔔 ⋯' @1310. The component's 9-child anatomy (btn/exit '‹ Exit', site name, pill/saved, pill/in, spacer, presence, btn/notifications, btn/publish, btn/more) has no Publish-less state, no 'Back to editing' label and no lifecycle pill. The only other 1440x56 local bar, 807:8724 'review-toolbar' in 807:8723, is a different surface entirely (external reviewer: site name, In review, page links, Request changes, Approve) and that board is already named ENTRY POINT.
recommend: Add a third variant axis Mode = {edit, view} to 681:122. In Mode=view: btn/exit swaps label to '‹ Back to editing', btn/publish and pill/saved hide, and the pill slot becomes the lifecycle pill. Then swap 1343:7163 for an instance. Leave 807:8724 as its own component — it belongs with the client-review chrome in D-N-12.

finding: Two boards in the same S1.6 family draw contradictory topbars for the same state, and neither is marked superseded. A reader cannot tell what a viewer actually sees.
evidence: 813:4676 'S1.6 · viewer-editor-state · read-only-chrome' carries a full standard Topbar instance 813:4677 whose children include btn/publish reading 'Publish', pill/saved 'Saved 2m ago', presence and btn/notifications — i.e. the complete editing bar, on a board whose name says read-only. 1343:7162 'S1.6 · view-mode · stripped-chrome — NEW 2026-08-28' draws 1343:7163 with no Publish, no save pill, and '‹ Back to editing'. Both live in section 23 · Journeys; only 813:4676 predates the 08-28 board.
recommend: Founder call on which S1.6 is the design of record, then rename the loser with a SUPERSEDED prefix (never delete). If the 08-28 board wins, 813:4676's instance should move to Mode=view once D-N-03 lands.

finding: Five of the six variant cells are load-bearing; one is used by no screen anywhere. The Publish x Review axis pair is the right shape, but Publish=anyway is nearly dead and pairs with Review=none never.
evidence: Page 1:3, per-instance mainComponent name: Publish=disabled,Review=open 74; Publish=ready,Review=open 22; Publish=disabled,Review=none 3; Publish=anyway,Review=open 2; Publish=ready,Review=none 1; Publish=anyway,Review=none 0. Page 1:2 holds 19 more instances inside 'holder' frames (8/7/1/1/1/1) — documentation, not screens. So Publish=anyway,Review=none (681:103) is referenced exactly once file-wide and only by its own spec holder.
recommend: Keep the cell — a 3x2 set with one unused corner is cheaper than an asymmetric set, and 'publish anyway with no review open' is a state the product can reach. No action; recorded so the next census does not read 0 as rot.

finding: Review=open is the de-facto default: 98 of 102 topbars show the 'In review' pill, so first-run, offline, loading, template-picking and all twelve Settings screens each assert that a client review is open. The axis default is inverted relative to the product, where an open review is the agency exception, not the resting state.
evidence: Review=open on 98 instances (74 Publish=disabled + 22 Publish=ready + 2 Publish=anyway); Review=none on 4 (3 disabled + 1 ready). The pill is child 681:35 'pill/in' 129x22 reading 'In review · 3 open', visible=true in Review=open and visible=false in Review=none (verified by comparing 681:26 against 681:65, where the pill is visible=false and the spacer widens from 680 to 821). Boards asserting an open review include 65:2 Shell state 1 · First run, 66:441 Shell state 10 · Offline, 65:412 Shell state 12 · Loading, 642:2556 Templates · preview, and 638:2378 through 640:3849 (all twelve S7 Settings screens).
recommend: This is not sample-data copy — the pill's presence is a state claim. Flip the set's defaultValue for Review to 'none', then re-set Review=open only on the S5 review boards (128:2 through 133:630, plus 200:213 Shell state 8 · Review active) and anywhere a board's own name says a review is open. Roughly 90 instances change.

finding: Every one of the 102 instances overrides fills AND strokes — because the instances are bound to design variables and the six masters are not. The tokens live on the copies, so a colour change made on the component will never reach a single board, and Figma now records a permanent paint override on all 102.
evidence: Master 681:27 fills = SOLID {r:1,g:1,b:1} with boundVariables {}; strokes = SOLID #F3F4F6 with boundVariables {}. All six variants read the same: 681:26/27/46/65/84/103 all fillBound={} strokeBound={}. Sampled instances 682:2657, 682:5201, 813:4677, 682:5026, 682:5756 all carry the identical colour but bound — fill to VariableID:2:10 (color/bg-panel), stroke to VariableID:524:60 (flowbite/gray/100). Override-field tally across the 102: fills 102, strokes 102, reactions 55, characters 4, height 1, width 1, visible 1.
recommend: Bind color/bg-panel and flowbite/gray/100 on all six masters, then reset the fill/stroke override on the 102 instances. Until that is done, the topbar's surface colour is unmaintainable from the component and 'the gated token is the dead copy' all over again.

finding: The topbar's two instance-swap slots exist, are fully designed, and are never used. Save status has 6 states and Presence has 5 — 9 designed states with zero uses — so the Offline shell and the Saving-to-conflict shell both display 'Saved 2m ago' and a solo presence avatar. The boards contradict their own names.
evidence: 681:122 componentPropertyDefinitions: 'Save#698:0' INSTANCE_SWAP default 697:444, 'Presence#695:0' INSTANCE_SWAP default 692:421. Across all 102 instances the swap tally is Save=697:444 x102 and Presence=692:421 x102 — no instance differs from the default. The sets those defaults come from: 697:461 'Save status' = State=saved(697:444)/saving(697:448)/unsaved(697:452)/conflict(697:456)/offline(697:460)/error(701:2); 692:472 'Presence' = State=solo(692:421)/few/many/reconnecting/offline. Affected boards include 66:441 'Shell state 10 · Offline', 66:640 'Shell state 11 · Saving → conflict', 297:2139 'S1.2 · load-error', 807:7000 'S1.2e - Offline - Connection restored (syncing)', and 642:3696 '[design-ahead] Shell state 13 · Presence (multi…)'. Board 813:4836 'S1.2f · save-indicator · 5-states' draws the save states as a strip that no screen consumes.
recommend: Set Save on the ~6 boards whose names name a save state (offline, conflict, syncing, load-error, saving) and Presence on the multiplayer boards (642:3696, 963:4474, 200:213). This is the highest-value hour in the topbar: five designed states become visible on the screens that were drawn to show them.

finding: None of the six masters carries a single reaction, so every topbar's prototype wiring has to be redrawn per instance — and 47 of 102 never were. On those boards Exit, Publish, notifications and ⋯ are dead, including all thirteen 'Shell state' boards, which are the file's canonical editor screens.
evidence: Walked every descendant of 681:26/27/46/65/84/103: reactions = 0 on all six. Of the 102 instances, 55 carry at least one reaction somewhere inside and 47 carry none. The 47 include 65:2 Shell state 1, 199:2 Shell state 2, 199:205 Shell state 3, 66:4 Shell state 4, 199:409 Shell state 5, 200:2 Shell state 6, 65:211 Shell state 7, 200:213 Shell state 8, 66:225 Shell state 9, 66:441 Shell state 10, 66:640 Shell state 11, 65:412 Shell state 12, 642:3696 Shell state 13, plus 128:2/129:2/129:451/130:2/130:201/130:400/130:599/130:798/130:997/131:2/131:201/131:415 (the S5 review family), 55:2, 58:2, 807:4299, 807:6694, 813:4676.
recommend: Put the reactions on the masters — btn/exit → the dashboard board, btn/publish → the publish flow, btn/more → 642:3401 Site menu (⋯), btn/notifications → 165:2 Notifications · unread. Instance-level reactions then become the exception rather than the only wiring, and 47 boards gain four working hotspots each without being touched.

finding: The one responsive shell resizes the topbar instance by hand because the component has no width story. It is the only instance in the file that is not 1440x56.
evidence: 682:5026 on board 202:2 is 1280x56 and its override set includes both 'width' and 'height' — the only instance of the 102 with either. The other 101 are 1440x56 at 0,0. The component's inner geometry is absolutely placed (btn/publish at x=1303, btn/more at x=1396 on a 1440 master), so a manual resize leaves the right cluster wherever the resize put it.
recommend: Give 681:122 horizontal auto-layout with the 'spacer' child (681:38) set to fill, so 1280 and 1440 both compose correctly and the resize stops being an override. Cheap, and it also fixes the Publish=anyway cell, whose spacer is hand-shortened to 625 to make room for the wider button.

finding: The Topbar component reaches page 1:3 and its own spec page and nothing else. Six other pages draw a full-width bar entirely by hand — 127 local bars counted — but they are different subjects, not detached editor topbars, so this is a component-inventory gap rather than topbar drift.
evidence: Instances of 681:122 by page: 1:3 = 102, 1:2 = 19 (spec holders), and 0 on 1:4, 1:5, 1:6, 1:7, 397:2 and 988:2. Local full-width bars 44-72px tall on those pages, counted by walking every descendant: 1:4 'Header' 1440x56 x47; 1:5 'Header' 1440x56 x32; 988:2 'Header' 1440x64 x9 + 'Public bar' 1440x56 x5 + 'Page header' 1200x56/58 x7 + four unnamed 1200-wide 48/56/58/66 bars x8; 397:2 'Topbar' 1440x56 x14; 1:7 'Topbar' 1440x56 x3 and 1280x56 x2 (archive). Pages 500:2 and 510:2 were not scanned — both are archived foreign kits.
recommend: Do not point these at 681:122 — they are site, dashboard and portfolio chrome, not the editor bar. Log them for the dashboard/site component arc; the 47 on 1:4 in particular sit on a page already recommended for retirement in D-J-01.

finding: The client-review surface has the exact disease the rail just had: its three chrome bars are hand-drawn 49 times with zero components. This is the next component after the topbar, and it is a larger duplication than the rail was.
evidence: Page 1:6, walked every descendant: 39 chrome bars, 0 INSTANCE. 'Branded bar' 1280x56 x16 in 3 signature groups (13 with 3 children reading 'Ali's Studio | Reviewing: Bella Cuci…', 2 with 4 children, 1 with 4 + 'Welcome back, Sara.'); 'Mode strip' 1280x44 x10, all one signature ('Preview | Comment | view-only'); 'Sticky footer' 1280x72 x10 in 5 signature groups (7x 'Request changes / ✓ Approve v3', plus changes-requested, approved, and post-approval-edited wordings); 'Agency header' 1280x56 x3. Page 1:3 adds 10 more 'Agency header' 1280x56 on the Client sign-off echo boards 1339:7163/7172/7187/7194/7201/7208/7215/7222 and 1340:7163/7175.

The five footer wordings map 1:1 to the five states already drawn, so the set can be built by promotion rather than redesign.

finding: There is no Inspector component and no part of one. Every right panel in the file is a hand-drawn local frame — 53 inside the editor shells and 18 standalone in the module — and 25 of the module's 26 boards contain not a single component instance of any kind.
evidence: Of the 53 boards >=1200 wide that draw a right-edge panel, 0 contain an INSTANCE as that panel (checked mainComponent on every instance in every board). Inside section 1776:8381, per-board instance census: 25 of 26 boards return NO INSTANCES; the sole exception is 32:2, which contains three icons (Icon / link, Icon / corner-left-up, Icon / crosshair). Page 1:2's library holds 20 COMPONENT_SETs and 50 COMPONENTs — Row, Button, Input, Badge, Topbar, Rail, Panel header, Section header, Tree row, List row, Version row, Record row, Card / media — and the Inspector uses none of them. For contrast the same page-1:3 walk finds 1,597 instances overall: 585 Settings nav row, 190 Button, 156 Panel header, 102 Topbar, 99 Rail, 65 Section header, 57 Tree row, 44 List row.
recommend: Build it. See D-N-20 for the axis. Until then every Inspector change is 71 manual edits, which is why the geometry in D-N-15 has already drifted ten ways.

finding: Width is the one thing the Inspector has not drifted on. Every right panel in the file is 300 wide, matching the shipping code. There is no second width to reconcile.
evidence: Measured the right-edge panel on all 50 boards that are exactly 1440x900 and draw one: width = 300 on 50 of 50. Across the whole module, every panel board is 300 wide (807:8342/8412/8475/8521/8567/8614, 32:2, 159:99/102/123, 160:2/105/208/313/412/512, 189:2, 1707:8456, 824:5095, 1175:4841, 159:2). The only non-300 nodes in the section are popovers and a modal, which are not panels: 1176:4804 236x184, 1707:8406 228x162, 1707:8417 240x113, 1707:8427 240x158, 1706:8458 720x132, 429:2350 1120x701. Two 280-wide hits in an earlier pass were left-hand Drawers (807:4299 'Drawer (Templates)', 807:6558 'Drawer (Insert)'), not inspectors.
recommend: Freeze 300 as the Inspector width in the component. No boards need changing.

finding: The Inspector's vertical extent is drawn ten different ways on fifty otherwise-identical shells, and on eleven of them the panel stops short of the footer, leaving a gap that appears on no other board. Width held because it is one number; height drifted because nothing enforces it.
evidence: Geometry of the right panel on the 50 boards that are exactly 1440x900: heights 812 (29), 768 (10), 780 (2), 778 (2), 748 (2), 772 (1), 744 (1), 736 (1), 702 (1), 560 (1). Top edge y=56 on 38 boards and y=100 on 12 (the S5 review family 129:223, 129:451, 130:201, 130:400, 130:599, 131:415, 132:2, 133:2, 133:212, 133:422, 133:630, 200:213 — those insert a review strip under the topbar). Bottom edge is 868 (= 900 − 32 footer) on 39 boards; the other 11 stop at 836 (297:1972, 66:4, 132:2), 834 (128:2, 297:2027), 828 (807:7000), 804 (65:2, 66:640), 802 (130:201), 800 (813:4676) and 616 (807:6694 — 252px of empty board below the panel). Within the module itself the same drift shows as 300x812 on 17 boards, 300x776 on 32:2, 300x552 on 824:5095, 300x169 on 1175:4841.
recommend: Lock the panel to y=56, height 812, bottom 868 in the component and let the S5 review family be the single documented exception at y=100/height 768. Fix 807:6694 first — a 560-high inspector on a 900 board is visible at a glance.

finding: The module is built by two hands with two conventions: the six element-type profiles are absolutely-positioned frames, every other Inspector board is auto-layout. They cannot become one component until they agree.
evidence: layoutMode read on each board. NONE (absolute): 807:8342 TEXT (58 children), 807:8412 FLEX (49), 807:8475 GRID (38), 807:8521 MEDIA (38), 807:8567 BUTTON (38), 807:8614 INPUT (36). VERTICAL (auto-layout): 32:2 CONTAINER (25), 824:5095 flat scroll body (22), 159:99 no-selection (2), 159:123 multi-select (9), 160:2 instance-selected (19), 160:105 bound-to-CMS (19), 160:208, 160:313, 160:412, 160:512, 189:2, 1707:8456. The absolute boards also name their children by content ('TYPOGRAPHY', 'Family', 'Frame') while the auto-layout boards name them by role ('row', 'Row · Background', 'Bound note').
recommend: Rebuild the six profile boards as vertical auto-layout columns of one 'Inspector / Section row' component before any component work starts. This is the prerequisite for D-N-20, not a separate cleanup.

finding: The profile boards and the shipping profile map agree on the seven profiles and on section order, but every board is one section out of step with the code, and the MEDIA board draws a section its own code comment says was removed.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/inspector/config/elementProfiles.ts defines exactly seven profiles — CONTAINER, TEXT, FLEX, GRID, MEDIA, BUTTON, INPUT — matching the seven boards 32:2, 807:8342, 807:8412, 807:8475, 807:8521, 807:8567, 807:8614 one-to-one (not ten; the brief's '10 profiles' is a miscount). Every code profile ends with 'all-css', which no profile board draws: board section counts are TEXT 12, FLEX 13, GRID 13, MEDIA 12, BUTTON 13, INPUT 12 against code lengths 13, 14, 14, 13, 14, 13. Separately, 807:8521 MEDIA draws a section header literally named 'LINK — Link section is not…' while MEDIA_PROFILE has no 'link' entry at all and its code comment explains why ('LinkSection's own gate is link/button/a/cta … only inflated the footer's denominator past the board's of 12').
recommend: 'all-css' renders only in dev (sections/registry/__tests__/shouldRender.test.ts:36), so the boards are right to omit it — record that as a deliberate exception in the board notes rather than adding a row. Delete the LINK header from 807:8521, which is a leftover the code already retired.

finding: Every profile board's footer says 'N of M sections apply' while the board lists all M sections on screen. The number is counting what is expanded, and the word is telling the user what is relevant — so the footer contradicts the body it sits under.
evidence: 807:8342 TEXT: footer '2 of 12 sections apply', 12 section headers drawn, 2 carrying the expanded chevron 'v' (TYPOGRAPHY, SPACING). 807:8412 FLEX: '4 of 13', 13 drawn, 4 expanded (LAYOUT, FLEXBOX, SIZE, SPACING). 807:8475 GRID '2 of 13', 807:8521 MEDIA '2 of 12', 807:8567 BUTTON '2 of 13', 807:8614 INPUT '2 of 12' — each numerically self-consistent with its expanded count. The code agrees that expansion is value-driven, not applicability-driven: elementProfiles.ts:29-33 says 'Which of them open on first sight is not encoded here — that is whichever sections carry a value on the element … which is what every profile board's footer counts.'
recommend: Change the copy to match what it counts — '2 sections have values' or '2 of 12 sections in use'. 'apply' promises a filtered list the panel does not deliver.

finding: The container fallback — the profile every unmapped element type lands on, and therefore the most-seen panel in the product — is the least finished board in the module. It is the wrong height, shows six of its sixteen sections, and has no footer at all.
evidence: 32:2 is 300x776 where every other panel board is 300x812. Its 16 rows read: header, breadcrumb (This ▾ / Desktop ▾ / Base ▾), LAYOUT + Display + Size, SPACING + Padding + Gap, TYPOGRAPHY + Family + Size, BACKGROUND + Fill, BORDER + Radius, EFFECTS + Opacity — six sections, all expanded, no collapsed tail and no 'N of M' footer. CONTAINER_PROFILE in elementProfiles.ts orders sixteen: layout, flex, grid, size, spacing, typography, background, border, corner-radius, effects, interactions, animation, visibility, element-properties, css-classes, all-css. The board omits ten of them. It is also the only profile board built in VERTICAL auto-layout (see D-N-16) and the only one holding component instances.
recommend: Redraw 32:2 at 300x812 with all sixteen rows and a footer, matching the six sibling profiles. Because it is the fallback, it is what a user sees for every element type the map does not name — the fallback should be the most complete board in the module, not the thinnest.

finding: One component set with a single axis Profile = {container, text, flex, grid, media, button, input} is the right build, because the seven profiles differ in exactly four things and none of them is geometry. Selection state must NOT be a second axis on the same set.
evidence: Structure read on all seven boards. Identical across all of them: panel 300 wide; a 'header' frame 300x48 at y=0 (first child of 807:8342/8412/8475/8521/8567/8614 and of 32:2, 159:102, 160:208, 160:313, 160:412, 189:2 — text read on 807:8342 as 'Text | ✦ AI | ⋯' and on 32:2 as '⬚ Section | ✦ AI | ⋯'); a 300x32 context row at y=48 (text read on 32:2 as 'This ▾ / Desktop ▾ / Base ▾'); a 28px section-row pitch; a collapsed row = 16px label + 7x12 chevron '>'; an expanded row = 15px label + a 160x28 control, or 80+72 for paired values; a 300x13 footer. What actually differs, and only this: (1) the ordered list of section ids — TEXT starts typography/spacing, FLEX layout/flex, GRID layout/grid, MEDIA size/spacing, BUTTON typography/background, INPUT typography/border; (2) which rows carry 'v' rather than '>'; (3) the header glyph and type label; (4) the footer denominator. The vocabulary is a fixed set of 16 section ids shared by all seven (SectionId in sections/registry/_shared.tsx).
recommend: Build bottom-up: (a) 'Inspector / Section row' component set, axis State = {collapsed, expanded}, with a text property for the label and a slot for the control block; (b) 'Inspector / Panel', 300x812, vertical auto-layout = header + context row + a slot for the row column + footer; (c) Profile as a 7-value variant axis on the Panel only if the founder wants the seven orders frozen in Figma — otherwise seven instances with reordered children, which stays truer to elementProfiles.ts being the SSOT for order. Do NOT make State a second axis: 7 profiles x 11 states = 77 cells of which ~11 exist, and the state boards carry no element type at all (multi-select and no-selection have no profile).

finding: The eleven selection-state boards belong in a second component set, and three of them break the shared header the other eight keep — worth deciding deliberately rather than by drift.
evidence: Eight state boards open with the standard 300x48 header row: 159:102 loading, 160:2 instance-selected, 160:105 bound-to-CMS, 160:208 breakpoint-override, 160:313 pseudo-state, 160:412 reach-all-like-this, 189:2 reach-whole-site, 159:123 multi-select (its own 'Header' 300x48). Three do not: 159:99 no-selection opens with 'Empty state' 300x160 ('Select something on the canvas / ✦ Ask AI ›'), 1707:8456 error-boundary opens with 'Error card' 276x106 ('Inspector Error / Unknown error / Try Again'), 160:512 ai-agent-run opens with 'Back row' 300x36 ('‹  Inspector'). 159:2 'Inspector · single-selection' is already marked RETIRED 2026-09-02.
recommend: Second set 'Inspector / State' with axis State = {no-selection, loading, multi-select, instance-selected, bound-to-CMS, breakpoint-override, pseudo-state, reach-all-like-this, reach-whole-site, ai-agent-run, error-boundary}. Keep the header on the eight that have it; the three that replace it are replacing the whole panel, which is legitimate — say so in the board names so a future census does not read it as drift.

finding: The library already owns the two primitives the Inspector needs, but both are sized for the left drawer, which is the mechanical reason the Inspector could never adopt them. Section header is additionally resized three different ways by the boards that do use it.
evidence: 16:6 'Panel header' master 280x44 — 156 instances on page 1:3, every one of them exactly 280x44, never resized. 16:16 'Section header' master 320x28 — 65 instances at three sizes and never at its own: 280x28 x42, 360x28 x16, 640x28 x7. The Inspector's own header is 300x48 and its section rows sit at 300 wide, so neither master fits without a resize. 19:47 'Right panel frame' — the one component whose name promises this job — is 360x776 with a 360x48 header, i.e. drawer-sized, and has 0 instances on page 1:3. 8:47 'Row' (20 variants, Size x State) also has 0 instances on page 1:3.
recommend: Give both masters horizontal auto-layout with a filling label so 280/300/320/360/640 are all one component, and either resize 19:47 'Right panel frame' to 300 or rename it 'Drawer frame (360)' so it stops reading as the Inspector's shell. Four components with zero or wrong-width uses is a library that has been written but not adopted — the same failure the Inspector itself shows at scale.
